title: Delete Characters to Make Fancy String
notes:
Task and constraints: Remove characters so no three consecutive characters are equal.
Idea: `makeFancyString` scans characters in order and appends a character only when doing so would not make the last three output characters equal.
Technique and why it applies: Checking the last two output characters prevents a third identical character from entering the result.
Invariant: The output prefix never contains three identical consecutive characters, and each accepted character preserves original order.
Edge cases: Runs of length one or two are retained; longer runs are truncated to two; empty input returns empty output.
Complexity: O(n) time and O(n) output space.
complexity_reason: Checking the last two output characters prevents a third identical character from entering the result.

title: Delete Characters to Make Fancy String
notes:
Task and constraints: Remove characters so no three consecutive characters are equal.
Idea: `makeFancyString` scans characters in order and appends a character only when doing so would not make the last three output characters equal.
Technique and why it applies: Checking the last two output characters prevents a third identical character from entering the result.
Invariant: The output prefix never contains three identical consecutive characters, and each accepted character preserves original order.
Edge cases: Runs of length one or two are retained; longer runs are truncated to two; empty input returns empty output.
Complexity: O(n) time and O(n) output space.
code: class Solution { public String makeFancyString(String s){StringBuilder b=new StringBuilder();for(char c:s.toCharArray()){int n=b.length();if(n<2||b.charAt(n-1)!=c||b.charAt(n-2)!=c)b.append(c);}return b.toString();} }
complexity_reason: Checking the last two output characters prevents a third identical character from entering the result.

title: Check If String Is a Prefix of Array
notes:
Task and constraints: Return true if s equals the concatenation of a nonempty prefix of words.
Idea: `isPrefixString` appends successive `words` to a builder and compares the accumulated text to `s`, returning true on exact equality and false once it exceeds or diverges.
Technique and why it applies: Comparing after each appended word ensures the match ends exactly at a word boundary.
Invariant: After each iteration the builder is the concatenation of a nonempty prefix of `words`.
Edge cases: A matching prefix must end at a word boundary; exhausting all words without equality returns false; empty `words` cannot form a nonempty prefix.
Complexity: O(total characters) time and O(|s|) to O(total input) auxiliary space depending on the builder implementation.
complexity_reason: Comparing after each appended word ensures the match ends exactly at a word boundary.

title: Check If String Is a Prefix of Array
notes:
Task and constraints: Return true if s equals the concatenation of a nonempty prefix of words.
Idea: `isPrefixString` appends successive `words` to a builder and compares the accumulated text to `s`, returning true on exact equality and false once it exceeds or diverges.
Technique and why it applies: Comparing after each appended word ensures the match ends exactly at a word boundary.
Invariant: After each iteration the builder is the concatenation of a nonempty prefix of `words`.
Edge cases: A matching prefix must end at a word boundary; exhausting all words without equality returns false; empty `words` cannot form a nonempty prefix.
Complexity: O(total characters) time and O(|s|) to O(total input) auxiliary space depending on the builder implementation.
code: class Solution { public boolean isPrefixString(String s,String[] words){StringBuilder b=new StringBuilder();for(String w:words){b.append(w);if(b.toString().equals(s))return true;if(b.length()>=s.length())return false;}return false;} }
complexity_reason: Comparing after each appended word ensures the match ends exactly at a word boundary.

title: Number of Strings That Appear as Substrings in Word
approach_name: Count patterns contained in the word
notes:
Task and constraints: Count patterns that occur as substrings of word.
Idea: `numOfStrings` tests each pattern with substring containment in `word` and increments the count for every match.
Technique and why it applies: Each pattern contributes one exactly when the full pattern is contained somewhere in the word.
Invariant: The counter equals the number of patterns processed so far that occur at least once in `word`.
Edge cases: A pattern is counted once even if it appears multiple times; overlapping occurrences do not increase its contribution.
Complexity: O(sum of pattern lengths times the word-search cost) time and O(1) auxiliary space beyond inputs.
code:
class Solution:
 def numOfStrings(self,patterns,word):return sum(p in word for p in patterns)
complexity_reason: Each pattern contributes one exactly when the full pattern is contained somewhere in the word.

title: Number of Strings That Appear as Substrings in Word
approach_name: Count patterns contained in the word
notes:
Task and constraints: Count patterns that occur as substrings of word.
Idea: `numOfStrings` tests each pattern with substring containment in `word` and increments the count for every match.
Technique and why it applies: Each pattern contributes one exactly when the full pattern is contained somewhere in the word.
Invariant: The counter equals the number of patterns processed so far that occur at least once in `word`.
Edge cases: A pattern is counted once even if it appears multiple times; overlapping occurrences do not increase its contribution.
Complexity: O(sum of pattern lengths times the word-search cost) time and O(1) auxiliary space beyond inputs.
code: class Solution { public int numOfStrings(String[] patterns,String word){int n=0;for(String p:patterns)if(word.contains(p))n++;return n;} }
complexity_reason: Each pattern contributes one exactly when the full pattern is contained somewhere in the word.

title: Find if Path Exists in Graph
notes:
Task and constraints: Return whether an undirected path exists between source and destination.
Idea: Build adjacency lists for both directions, then run DFS or BFS from `source` and return whether `destination` is visited.
Technique and why it applies: Graph traversal reaches every vertex connected to the source and stops revisiting nodes through the visited set.
Invariant: The visited set contains precisely vertices discovered from the source during the graph traversal.
Edge cases: A source equal to destination is reachable; disconnected vertices remain unvisited; edges are undirected and may lead to already visited nodes.
Complexity: O(n+m) time and O(n+m) space for adjacency lists and traversal state.
complexity_reason: Graph traversal reaches every vertex connected to the source and stops revisiting nodes through the visited set.

title: Find if Path Exists in Graph
notes:
Task and constraints: Return whether an undirected path exists between source and destination.
Idea: Build adjacency lists for both directions, then run DFS or BFS from `source` and return whether `destination` is visited.
Technique and why it applies: Graph traversal reaches every vertex connected to the source and stops revisiting nodes through the visited set.
Invariant: The visited set contains precisely vertices discovered from the source during the graph traversal.
Edge cases: A source equal to destination is reachable; disconnected vertices remain unvisited; edges are undirected and may lead to already visited nodes.
Complexity: O(n+m) time and O(n+m) space for adjacency lists and traversal state.
code:
import java.util.*;
class Solution { public boolean validPath(int n,int[][] edges,int source,int destination){List<List<Integer>>g=new ArrayList<>();for(int i=0;i<n;i++)g.add(new ArrayList<>());for(int[]e:edges){g.get(e[0]).add(e[1]);g.get(e[1]).add(e[0]);}boolean[]seen=new boolean[n];ArrayDeque<Integer>st=new ArrayDeque<>();st.push(source);seen[source]=true;while(!st.isEmpty()){int x=st.pop();if(x==destination)return true;for(int y:g.get(x))if(!seen[y]){seen[y]=true;st.push(y);}}return false;} }
complexity_reason: Graph traversal reaches every vertex connected to the source and stops revisiting nodes through the visited set.

title: Minimum Time to Type Word Using Special Typewriter
notes:
Task and constraints: Compute the minimum time to type the word on a circular alphabet dial, including one press per character.
Idea: For each character, compute the circular alphabet distance `d=abs(ord(ch)-pos)` and add `min(d,26-d)+1` for movement plus pressing.
Technique and why it applies: Taking the minimum of direct and wraparound distances gives the shortest dial movement for every character.
Invariant: `pos` records the previous character position; each step chooses the shorter clockwise or counterclockwise path and pays one second to type the character.
Edge cases: The initial pointer is at `a`; wrapping from `z` to `a` is one step; every character incurs a press.
Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity_reason: Taking the minimum of direct and wraparound distances gives the shortest dial movement for every character.

title: Minimum Time to Type Word Using Special Typewriter
notes:
Task and constraints: Compute the minimum time to type the word on a circular alphabet dial, including one press per character.
Idea: For each character, compute the circular alphabet distance `d=abs(ord(ch)-pos)` and add `min(d,26-d)+1` for movement plus pressing.
Technique and why it applies: Taking the minimum of direct and wraparound distances gives the shortest dial movement for every character.
Invariant: `pos` records the previous character position; each step chooses the shorter clockwise or counterclockwise path and pays one second to type the character.
Edge cases: The initial pointer is at `a`; wrapping from `z` to `a` is one step; every character incurs a press.
Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
code: class Solution { public int minTimeToType(String word){int pos=0,ans=0;for(char c:word.toCharArray()){int next=c-'a',d=Math.abs(next-pos);ans+=Math.min(d,26-d)+1;pos=next;}return ans;} }
complexity_reason: Taking the minimum of direct and wraparound distances gives the shortest dial movement for every character.

title: Find Greatest Common Divisor of Array
notes:
Task and constraints: Return the greatest common divisor of the smallest and largest array values.
Idea: Find the minimum and maximum array values, then return their Euclidean GCD using repeated remainder operations.
Technique and why it applies: Only the minimum and maximum are needed by the problem, and Euclid's algorithm computes their GCD efficiently.
Invariant: The GCD result divides both extrema and is the greatest positive divisor common to them.
Edge cases: The input values are positive; a one-element array has equal extrema; Euclid's algorithm terminates when the remainder becomes zero.
Complexity: O(n + log M) time and O(1) auxiliary space, where M is the maximum value.
complexity_reason: Only the minimum and maximum are needed by the problem, and Euclid's algorithm computes their GCD efficiently.

title: Find Greatest Common Divisor of Array
notes:
Task and constraints: Return the greatest common divisor of the smallest and largest array values.
Idea: Find the minimum and maximum array values, then return their Euclidean GCD using repeated remainder operations.
Technique and why it applies: Only the minimum and maximum are needed by the problem, and Euclid's algorithm computes their GCD efficiently.
Invariant: The GCD result divides both extrema and is the greatest positive divisor common to them.
Edge cases: The input values are positive; a one-element array has equal extrema; Euclid's algorithm terminates when the remainder becomes zero.
Complexity: O(n + log M) time and O(1) auxiliary space, where M is the maximum value.
code: class Solution { public int findGCD(int[] nums){int a=nums[0],b=nums[0];for(int x:nums){a=Math.min(a,x);b=Math.max(b,x);}while(b!=0){int t=a%b;a=b;b=t;}return a;} }
complexity_reason: Only the minimum and maximum are needed by the problem, and Euclid's algorithm computes their GCD efficiently.

title: Final Value of Variable After Performing Operations
notes:
Task and constraints: Return the final value starting from zero after applying each operation.
Idea: Start `x` at zero and increment for operations containing `++`; decrement for operations containing `--`.
Technique and why it applies: Each operation changes the accumulator by exactly one, so a single pass computes the final value.
Invariant: After each operation, `x` equals the variable's value after all operations processed so far.
Edge cases: The operation strings use the specified increment/decrement tokens; the initial value is zero; order does not affect the net count.
Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
code:
class Solution:
 def finalValueAfterOperations(self,operations):return sum(1 if '+' in x else -1 for x in operations)
complexity_reason: Each operation changes the accumulator by exactly one, so a single pass computes the final value.

Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
code: class Solution { public int finalValueAfterOperations(String[] operations){int ans=0;for(String s:operations)ans+=s.charAt(1)=='+'?1:-1;return ans;} }
complexity_reason: Each operation changes the accumulator by exactly one, so a single pass computes the final value.

title: Convert 1D Array Into 2D Array
notes:
Task and constraints: Reshape original into an m by n matrix, or return an empty array if sizes do not match.
Idea: Check whether `original.length == m*n`; if not, return an empty matrix, otherwise fill each output cell from the next row-major input position.
Technique and why it applies: A row-major index mapping reshapes the array without changing the order of its elements.
Invariant: The flattened output order matches the original array order, with row `r`, column `c` receiving `original[r*n+c]`.
Edge cases: If dimensions do not match the input size, no reshape is possible; zero dimensions follow the platform's matrix constraints.
Complexity: O(mn) time and O(mn) output space.
complexity_reason: A row-major index mapping reshapes the array without changing the order of its elements.

title: Convert 1D Array Into 2D Array
notes:
Task and constraints: Reshape original into an m by n matrix, or return an empty array if sizes do not match.
Idea: Check whether `original.length == m*n`; if not, return an empty matrix, otherwise fill each output cell from the next row-major input position.
Technique and why it applies: A row-major index mapping reshapes the array without changing the order of its elements.
Invariant: The flattened output order matches the original array order, with row `r`, column `c` receiving `original[r*n+c]`.
Edge cases: If dimensions do not match the input size, no reshape is possible; zero dimensions follow the platform's matrix constraints.
Complexity: O(mn) time and O(mn) output space.
code: class Solution { public int[][] construct2DArray(int[] original,int m,int n){if((long)m*n!=original.length)return new int[0][0];int[][]out=new int[m][n];for(int i=0;i<original.length;i++)out[i/n][i%n]=original[i];return out;} }
complexity_reason: A row-major index mapping reshapes the array without changing the order of its elements.

title: Two Out of Three
approach_name: Keep values present in at least two arrays
notes:
Task and constraints: Return distinct values that occur in at least two of the three arrays.
Idea: Convert each input array to a set, count in how many of the three sets each value appears, and return values with count at least two.
Technique and why it applies: Set membership counts arrays containing a value rather than raw occurrences, matching the distinct-value requirement.
Invariant: The membership count reflects distinct-array presence, so duplicates inside one array do not increase a value's cross-array count.
Edge cases: The output contains distinct values; a value present in all three arrays is included once; ordering is unspecified unless the code sorts it.
Complexity: O(n1+n2+n3+u) expected time and O(u) space for distinct values.
complexity_reason: Set membership counts arrays containing a value rather than raw occurrences, matching the distinct-value requirement.

title: Two Out of Three
approach_name: Keep values present in at least two arrays
notes:
Task and constraints: Return distinct values that occur in at least two of the three arrays.
Idea: Convert each input array to a set, count in how many of the three sets each value appears, and return values with count at least two.
Technique and why it applies: Set membership counts arrays containing a value rather than raw occurrences, matching the distinct-value requirement.
Invariant: The membership count reflects distinct-array presence, so duplicates inside one array do not increase a value's cross-array count.
Edge cases: The output contains distinct values; a value present in all three arrays is included once; ordering is unspecified unless the code sorts it.
Complexity: O(n1+n2+n3+u) expected time and O(u) space for distinct values.
code:
import java.util.*;
class Solution { public List<Integer> twoOutOfThree(int[] nums1,int[] nums2,int[] nums3){Set<Integer>a=new HashSet<>(),b=new HashSet<>(),c=new HashSet<>();for(int x:nums1)a.add(x);for(int x:nums2)b.add(x);for(int x:nums3)c.add(x);Set<Integer>out=new TreeSet<>();for(int x:a)if(b.contains(x)||c.contains(x))out.add(x);for(int x:b)if(c.contains(x))out.add(x);return new ArrayList<>(out);} }
complexity_reason: Set membership counts arrays containing a value rather than raw occurrences, matching the distinct-value requirement.

title: Minimum Number of Moves to Seat Everyone
notes:
Task and constraints: Return the total absolute movement needed to assign each student to a seat.
Idea: Sort `seats` and `students`, then sum `abs(seats[i]-students[i])` for each paired index.
Technique and why it applies: Matching sorted ranks is optimal for absolute-distance assignment because crossing pairs cannot improve total movement.
Invariant: After sorting both lists, pairing values at the same rank minimizes total absolute assignment distance.
Edge cases: The two arrays have equal length; duplicate positions are allowed; every student is assigned exactly one seat.
Complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) space if sorting copies are used.
code:
class Solution:
 def minMovesToSeat(self,seats,students):return sum(abs(a-b) for a,b in zip(sorted(seats),sorted(students)))
complexity_reason: Matching sorted ranks is optimal for absolute-distance assignment because crossing pairs cannot improve total movement.

title: Minimum Number of Moves to Seat Everyone
notes:
Task and constraints: Return the total absolute movement needed to assign each student to a seat.
Idea: Sort `seats` and `students`, then sum `abs(seats[i]-students[i])` for each paired index.
Technique and why it applies: Matching sorted ranks is optimal for absolute-distance assignment because crossing pairs cannot improve total movement.
Invariant: After sorting both lists, pairing values at the same rank minimizes total absolute assignment distance.
Edge cases: The two arrays have equal length; duplicate positions are allowed; every student is assigned exactly one seat.
Complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) space if sorting copies are used.
code:
import java.util.*;
class Solution { public int minMovesToSeat(int[] seats,int[] students){Arrays.sort(seats);Arrays.sort(students);int ans=0;for(int i=0;i<seats.length;i++)ans+=Math.abs(seats[i]-students[i]);return ans;} }
complexity_reason: Matching sorted ranks is optimal for absolute-distance assignment because crossing pairs cannot improve total movement.
